name: Cowpea Powdery Mildew
description: A fungal disease that forms white powdery growth on cowpea leaves, stems, and pods. It reduces photosynthetic capacity and can cause premature defoliation in severe cases.
symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on upper leaf surfaces
Yellowing and browning of affected leaves
Stunted growth and reduced pod production
Powdery growth may spread to stems and pods
causes: High nitrogen levels promoting succulent growth
treatments: Apply sulfur-based fungicides at first sign of infection
Spray neem oil solution (5ml/L water) weekly
Use potassium bicarbonate as organic treatment (1 tbsp/L water)
Apply myclobutanil or trifloxystrobin for severe cases
prevention: Space plants adequately for air circulation
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
